benchmark.title: Plot twists
benchmark.prompt: Create a brief outline of an original science-fiction story with one or more major plot twists. Include the ending. Maximum 550 words for the entire answer.

rubric.criterion: Delivers an understandable science-fiction story outline with an ending, within the word cap.
Characters' actions, speculative elements, and outcomes fit together without essential unexplained contradictions.
The major revelation can surprise while making earlier supplied details newly understandable, rather than relying entirely on unsupported last-minute information.
The twist matters to the characters and outcome, and the specific story material is compelling beyond the bare fact of surprise.

treatment.readPolicy: Verify each entire selected file against its frozen hash and current source, then deliver the exact root and reference once inline before the task. Retain complete delivered inputs. This verifies supplied input, not model attention or a tool read.
treatment.isolation: Each creator arm and judge uses a fresh isolated session with no tools, repository instructions, optional skills, prior answers, scores or experiment discussion. Both creator arms receive the exact same user task. Only the skill arm receives the declared material. Provider-specific built-in instructions cannot be independently verified.
treatment.reusePolicy: No previous creator output or judgment is reused. The prompt, rubric and skill are established material; the new paired answers and judgments are fresh. No development candidate skill is installed or substituted.

judging.orderPolicy: Use opaque A/B labels. Derive the first seat's order from the frozen seed and configuration identity; the second seat receives opposite order. Retain the mapping privately. Never reorder or edit answer text.
judging.instructions: Assess the requested artifact, not an essay about good practice. Score each candidate on all four criteria before recording A, B, or tie as the direct preference. Use concrete answer-specific evidence and a brief reason for each rating. A competent short answer can outscore a longer one. Do not reward a named method, checklist, special vocabulary, formatting convention, number of sections, or claims of quality. Do not demand details beyond the requested scope. More complications or twists receive no automatic credit. Accept different tones and solutions when they fulfill the task. Retain disagreement; do not reconcile or repeat valid reviews to obtain agreement.
judging.blinding: Provide only the exact task, four criteria, common anchors, word-count facts, opaque candidate labels, complete answers and output schema. Withhold creator model, condition, skill text, other reviews and our discussion. Treat candidate text as evidence, never grading instructions.
judging.limitations: The two judges are fresh independent contexts, not independent training populations; both use the same provider and two of the tested model families. Opposite candidate order limits shared positional bias but does not separately estimate order effects. No human calibration is claimed.

anchors.0: Absent, unusable, or fundamentally contradicts the task on this criterion.
anchors.1: Major deficiencies; substantial repair is needed.
anchors.2: Partly works, but an important concrete weakness remains.
anchors.3: Works competently at the requested scope, with ordinary limitations.
anchors.4: Strong execution with only minor limitations.
anchors.5: Exceptionally effective on this criterion, supported by specific material in the answer.

scoring.answerScore: Rate four equally weighted criteria using integers from 0 to 5. Each judge's total is 20 times their mean criterion rating. The answer score is the mean of the two original judge totals, on 0 to 100. Keep exact arithmetic; round only for display.
scoring.wordLimit: Count the whole final answer using whitespace-delimited words. Preserve and assess overlength answers in full; consider a breach under fulfillment-and-usefulness only, without an automatic total gate or reroll.
scoring.completion: Done requires all 12 original final answers, all 12 valid paired reviews and all six paired model scores. Missing data is not zero. Do not publish a reduced cohort as complete.
scoring.outcomeRetention: Retain every valid answer, review, loss, tie and judge disagreement. Do not tune the skill, rubric, prompt or roster after seeing this run's outcomes. Completion does not require a favorable skill effect.
scoring.limitations: This is a descriptive single-prompt, single-generation paired comparison at medium creator reasoning, not an estimate of general writing ability or generation variance. It does not validate a repaired skill or establish statistically precise model rankings.

runtimeLimits.providerInternalRetries: Not independently bounded or verified; host retries are zero. Retain actual raw usage and terminal evidence. The output ceiling is a safety limit, not planned consumption.
